creator: Iris

details.title: Tide Table Loom
details.description: A weaving draft that turns a week of harbour tides into a blue-and-rust border.
details.story: I drew the first repeat on the back of a ferry receipt. High water made a wide stripe, low water a narrow one. The corner of that receipt still has the coffee ring I used to trace the first curve.
details.original_goal: Weave a hand towel for each month of the fishing season.
details.abandonment_reason: The first towel took three Saturdays. By March I was still weaving January.
details.what_went_wrong: I made every centimetre of height a new row and spent most of the time changing thread.
details.what_could_be_improved: Keep the turning points and let the plain weave carry the hours between them.

updates: Found the original graph paper. The blue marks count warp threads, not hours.
Added the two-colour draft. The short rust floats were the only ones that survived the wash.
caption: Two-colour weave draft, with six tide peaks picked out in rust.

creator: Ada

details.title: Borrow a Bench
details.description: A ticket book for borrowing an empty workbench by the hour.
details.story: Three neighbours had tools and nowhere to use them. The cabinetmaker downstairs had the opposite problem. On Fridays we carried a tin of numbered tickets between the two buildings.
details.original_goal: Pay for the cabinetmaker’s heat and give beginners a place to learn.
details.abandonment_reason: The cabinetmaker moved, and none of our bookings covered the price of a new room.
details.what_went_wrong: We sold hour-long slots, but cleaning glue brushes and sweeping up took nearly half of each one.
details.what_could_be_improved: Try a single Saturday session with a shared cleanup at the end.

updates: I found the ticket stubs. Nine of the first twelve bookings were for exactly the same shelf repair.

creator: Luz

details.title: The Third Drawer
details.description: Nine unfinished stories told through the objects left in a kitchen drawer.
details.story: The first narrator was a bent whisk. It knew which cakes had fallen and which birthdays had been missed. By the time I reached the spare key, I had drawn three generations of the family on butcher paper.
details.original_goal: Tell one family history without letting a person narrate it.
details.abandonment_reason: The family tree became a second manuscript and I lost track of the first.
details.what_went_wrong: The objects all sounded like me. Even the oven mitt had an opinion about the mortgage.
details.what_could_be_improved: Start with the key and let it report only the doors it actually opened.

updates: Read the whisk story aloud. Cutting the last paragraph made the missing birthday much clearer.

creator: Tomas

details.title: Rain Ticket Press
details.description: A pavement rain gauge that prints a tiny receipt after a shower.
details.story: I wanted the first visitor after rain to find a slip of paper saying how much had fallen. An old till printer fit inside a biscuit tin, with an upturned funnel bolted to the lid.
details.original_goal: Build a rain gauge that could leave a paper record without a phone.
details.abandonment_reason: The rolls curled up in the damp long before the tin collected enough rain.
details.what_went_wrong: I waterproofed the electronics and left a generous slot for water beside the paper feed.
details.what_could_be_improved: Put the gauge outside and hand the readings to a printer indoors.

updates: The funnel still measures within a teaspoon of the kitchen jug. The tin is another story.

creator: Nell

details.title: Breadcrumb Radio
details.description: A walking tour that plays a neighbour’s recording when you reach the right corner.
details.story: At our first test the fishmonger told a story about a blackout. The listeners heard it a block early, beside a bright new pharmacy. Everybody remembered the pharmacy instead.
details.original_goal: Let a short walk unfold entirely through local voices.
details.abandonment_reason: We spent our last recording afternoon arguing with the location trigger.
details.what_went_wrong: Two parallel streets shared a GPS radius. Narrowing the circle made the recordings disappear indoors.
details.what_could_be_improved: Let the listener trigger each story by matching a detail on a printed card.

updates: Recovered four clean audio takes. The handwritten route includes a blue drainpipe that is still there.

details.title: Window Seat Index
details.description: A pocket index of things visible for less than a second from a train.
details.story: For a winter commute I kept one index card per window. A white horse made three appearances. A painted moon above a garage door appeared once, then scaffolding covered it for good.
details.original_goal: Make a field guide that another passenger could read on the same journey.
details.abandonment_reason: The timetable changed and my train began running in the dark.
details.what_went_wrong: I had written mile counts in one direction and minutes in the other.
details.what_could_be_improved: Pick a single daylight trip and put the landmarks in the order they appear.

creator: Iris

details.title: Ink Left on the Roller
details.description: A miniature print edition made entirely from the ink left after another print job.
details.story: I rolled the leftover green onto onion-skin paper and got the shape of a broken coastline. Other printers began saving their final pulls for me in a biscuit box.
details.original_goal: Make an edition of twenty maps from scraps other printers threw out.
details.abandonment_reason: Two sheets stuck together every time I tried to bind the book.
details.what_went_wrong: The pages looked dry but the thick bands of ink needed another week.
details.what_could_be_improved: Keep each print loose, with its own slip of tracing paper.

updates: Unpacked the biscuit box. Three clean prints survived between the old shopping lists.

creator: Ada

details.title: The Soup Shelf
details.description: A library of stockpots for neighbours cooking one very large meal.
details.story: The first borrower made broth for forty people after a choir rehearsal. She brought back the pot polished, with the recipe tucked under the lid. We kept the recipe and lost track of the lid.
details.original_goal: Share six oversized pots from one shop shelf.
details.abandonment_reason: Nobody could collect a heavy pot before the shop closed on weekdays.
details.what_went_wrong: Our sign-out cards tracked the pot and missed the lid, ladle and crate.
details.what_could_be_improved: Start with two complete kits. Give each kit its own crate and a Sunday return hour.

updates: The choir sent another recipe. Their note says the small pot serves twelve if nobody minds seconds.

creator: Nell

details.title: A Pantry in Pencil
details.description: A recipe search prototype that understood the names on my grandmother’s jars.
details.story: Her notes called chickpeas little buttons. I wrote a lookup table for the buttons, a second for the butter beans, and soon had a program that could cook in only one kitchen.
details.original_goal: Find a dinner from the handwritten labels in a cupboard.
details.abandonment_reason: I could never explain how to add another kitchen without rebuilding the dictionary.
details.what_went_wrong: A single label sometimes named the jar itself and sometimes what used to be in it.
details.what_could_be_improved: Ask the cook for one example dish when they add an ingredient.

updates: Found a label with three names crossed out. It belongs in the test cases.

creator: Noa

details.title: Pocket Loom Almanac
details.description: A postcard loom with one short weaving repeat for each change of tide.
details.story: Iris sent a photograph of her January towel. I cut twelve slots in a postcard and tried just the part where the tide turned. The first small sample took the length of a kettle boil.
details.original_goal: Make the tide draft small enough to finish on the ferry.
details.abandonment_reason: My first card bent in the middle as soon as I tightened the warp.
details.what_went_wrong: The long float on the back snagged on a coat button.
details.what_could_be_improved: I am testing folded card and a shorter float before drawing the next harbour.

updates: Folded two ticket stubs around the warp. The card stayed flat for the whole crossing.
The second sample fits in an envelope. I posted it back to Iris with the draft folded inside.
proposal: I can test one tide repeat on a postcard loom and send you the sample.

details.title: The Umbrella Drying Rack
details.description: A folding drip rack that almost fit under the counter of a six-seat café.
details.story: The owner measured the counter for me three times. We forgot to measure the umbrellas. On the first rainy morning the longest handle caught the till drawer.
details.original_goal: Get wet umbrellas out of the doorway without making a puddle at the counter.
details.abandonment_reason: The café changed hands before I could try the second set of hooks.
details.what_went_wrong: I built every slot for the same handle height.
details.what_could_be_improved: Angle the slots and make the drip tray removable from the side.

creator: Luz

details.title: The Platform Minute
details.description: A two-ink platform score in which every passing train leaves one mark.
details.story: I stood on the footbridge with a kitchen timer and two pencils. Local trains got a teal mark, expresses an orange one. When two passed at once, my pencil marks touched.
details.original_goal: Print one hour of station life on a single sheet.
details.abandonment_reason: I promised a whole week of observations before I had finished the first hour.
details.what_went_wrong: The first design made a quiet minute indistinguishable from a minute I missed.
details.what_could_be_improved: Give every minute a printed slot and mark a missed observation in pencil.

updates: I have set the first hour in a six-row grid. The empty slots finally read as silence.
caption: The first hour of observations. Teal marks local trains, orange marks expresses.

details.title: Return to Sender Club
details.description: A trial postcard subscription that paid for the stamp on the reply.
details.story: Six neighbours got the same question in the post. Four wrote back. The fifth walked over with her answer because she wanted to see who was asking.
details.original_goal: Fund a monthly exchange for people who liked writing letters.
details.abandonment_reason: I could pay for the outgoing post or the return post, but rarely both.
details.what_went_wrong: A subscription made a casual invitation feel like an assignment.
details.what_could_be_improved: Run one exchange at the library and sell the leftover cards individually.

details.title: Carbon Paper Weather
details.description: Working notes for a story told in the faint third copy of a weather report.
details.story: I found an envelope of carbon copies in a desk at a flea market. The pressure of the typist’s hand seemed to change with the weather.
details.original_goal: Write a short piece that could be read in any order.
details.abandonment_reason: The pages still need a beginning that earns the last image.
details.what_went_wrong: I kept describing the paper and forgetting the person at the typewriter.
details.what_could_be_improved: Try a version told by the person who collects the reports.
